name: tree-code-viewer

frames.best_why: Tree fully expanded with every file listed and the pricing-card source filling the code pane.

tagline: File tree on the left, highlighted source on the right, copy up top.
summary: A two-pane source browser: a collapsible file tree beside a syntax-highlighted code pane. Clicking a file swaps the code, folders expand, and a corner button copies the raw text.
appearance: A bordered two-column frame. The left column lists folders and files with small icons and guide lines, one row shaded for the selection; the right column shows monospace code with coloured keywords and a small copy button in its corner.
behaviour: Clicking a folder row expands or collapses it, while clicking a file row moves the selection and fades in that file's code. The copy button writes the raw source to the clipboard and swaps to a double tick for a moment.
demo_content: A pricing-card example project with pricing-card.tsx, use-billing-cycle.ts, button.tsx, utils.ts and package.json.
search_phrases: docs code pane with copy button
show a component and its dependencies
click a file to see its source
use_when: Documentation should show a component together with the several files it is built from.
avoid_when: It needs pre-highlighted HTML handed in, so the highlighter has to run before this renders.
customise: A files array with id, name, path, extension, raw text and pre-highlighted HTML drives it; default expansions and copy behaviour stay in the source.
weight_why: The viewer itself is light, but the demo pulls in a full syntax highlighter to build the HTML.

a11y.note: Tree rows and the copy control are click-only divs with no roles or labels, so nothing here is keyboard reachable.

issues: Frame 2 highlights a new file while the pane still shows the previous file's code.
Tree rows and the copy button are divs, so the viewer cannot be used from the keyboard.
polish_why: Crisp two-pane layout and readable highlighting; mouse-only controls are the main flaw.
